subject: Acuvera pilot: model recommendations, benchmarks & streaming UX concerns
messages:
From: Jordan Patel <jordan.patel@acuvera.com>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Liu <sara.liu@acuvera.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro / demo — follow-up and streaming behavior

Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — that was helpful. Two quick follow-ups from our product/eng team:

1) Model fit: can you recommend 2–3 candidate models we should evaluate for a clinical-notes summarization pilot (healthcare PII, 500–1,500 token inputs, target summary length ~120 tokens)? Speed matters — we want streaming partials in our UI within 150–250ms per chunk.

2) Streaming UX: we saw a few partial-output coherence issues during the demo (repeated phrases mid-stream, occasional early stop sequences). Can you share any known mitigations or prompt patterns that reduce these problems?

3) Benchmarks / artifacts: please share any benchmark reports or example prompt sets we can use to run an initial automated eval.

Attached is a rough scope (pilot_scope.xlsx) and a short sample of transcripts. Also, a reminder — we need the pilot timeline and a clear mutual action plan so we can align procurement and security review.

If you can send recommended models, expected latency profiles, and a proposed two-week pilot plan by EOD tomorrow that would be ideal.

Best,
Jordan
Product Manager, Acuvera Health

----
Attachment: pilot_scope.xlsx (spreadsheet with pilot milestones & sample datasets)

From: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Patel <jordan.patel@acuvera.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 16:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acuvera pilot: model recommendations, benchmarks & streaming UX concerns

Jordan — thanks for the clear ask and for the scope file. Quick recap and what we can deliver by EOD tomorrow:

Recap from our side
- Goal: 2-week pilot to validate model fit for clinical-notes summarization (PII-safe, high recall for key events, concise summary) + streaming UX within 150–250ms chunk latency.
- Key constraints: regulatory (PHI), on-prem or VPC deployment preferred for production; hosted pilot acceptable with SOC2/NDA protections.

Immediate recommendations (candidate models to evaluate)
- redwood-base-13b-q4f16: best cost/latency tradeoff for shorter summaries; robust with prefix caching for repeated contexts.
- redwood-clarion-33b-fp16: stronger coherence at slightly higher latency; better for complex context and medical terminology.
- redwood-guardian-70b-int8 (variant): if you need maximal quality, this gives best factuality but higher token cost — we can run a small A/B to confirm.

Streaming-specific mitigations we’ll include in the eval
- Stop-sequence tuning: avoid overly generic stop tokens; use targeted anchors (e.g., "\nPatient Summary:") and guard tokens to reduce premature termination.
- Partial-output coherence: enable micro-batching with KV cache warmup and prefix caching; we’ll run experiments on chunk sizes (64, 128 tokens) to find sweet spot between latency and continuity.
- Repeat suppression: apply simple repetition penalty / ngram-blocking heuristics in the runtime for streaming outputs.

Deliverables by EOD tomorrow
- A short benchmark package: bench-readme, example prompt sets (acuvera_prompt_set_v1.jsonl), and a small evaluation harness (SQuAD-style clinical QA + custom Q/A) — link below.
- Two-week pilot plan with mutual action plan (MAP) and milestones.
- Initial latency and throughput expectations per model (p95 token latency, tokens/sec on dedicated 1xA100).

Proposed timeline / MAP
- Day 0–2: access & dataset handoff (you provide sanitized sample set or we use sample provided).
- Day 3–5: run automated benchmarks + streaming experiments (stop sequences, 3 chunk sizes).
- Day 6: review results — pick 1 model variant for UX trial.
- Day 7–12: lightweight integration in your UI (streaming endpoint + client hooks).
- Day 13–14: collect qualitative feedback & final recap.

Action items
- Jordan: confirm which mode you prefer for pilot (hosted w/ SOC2 or VPC).
- Jordan: share any blocked/required stop tokens or UI-specific markers you need preserved.
- Rishi/Marissa: we’ll prepare the bench package and drive folder; Marissa to own integration support.

Links and artifacts
- Benchmark folder: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/rdw-4721/benchmarks
- Example prompt set: acuvera_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (attached)
- HubSpot: 2819-RDW-4721

I’ll attach the bench-readme and the prompt set now. If this looks good we’ll schedule a 45-min technical deep dive with our infra team for Friday.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Dylan — this is exactly the level of detail we need. A couple quick clarifications:

- We prefer a hosted pilot initially (SOC2 + enclosed dataset) to move faster; procurement will still need a 30-day security review.
- Our UI uses a chunk size of ~128 tokens by default; please prioritize that in your experiments.
- Can you call out expected p95 per-chunk latencies for the 13B vs 33B on a single A100? We need numbers to set product expectations.

Friday 11am PT for a 45-min technical deep dive works for our infra lead (Sara) and me. Please send calendar invite.

Jordan
Product Manager, Acuvera Health

Jordan / Sara — I’ll own the pilot run from the Redwood side and will prepare the benchmark harness for the 13B/33B variants with the 128-token chunk baseline.

Quick notes:
- Expected p95 per-chunk token latency (single A100, isolated):
  * redwood-base-13b-q4f16: ~110–160ms per 128-token chunk (depends on batch concurrency).
  * redwood-clarion-33b-fp16: ~220–320ms per 128-token chunk.
  * redwood-guardian-70b-int8: ~420–600ms per 128-token chunk (higher variance).

- We’ll include three stop-sequence configurations in the bench: conservative anchors, anchored token + guard, and permissive (to observe premature termination rates).
- I’ll drop the artifacts into the Drive folder and share edit access to your team.

Calendar invite: scheduled — Fri 11 Jun 2027 11:00–11:45 PT (includes infra deep dive link).

Regards,
Marissa Cole
